name: README.md
html:
luiskr.com V3 — cms

The content-management interface — the private admin surface behind the public site. cms/ is a completely separate bundle served under /cms, excluded from indexing (robots + X-Robots-Tag), and never shipped to public visitors.

Where website/ reads the Firebase translations/<locale>/ tree to render localized pages, cms/ is the tool that writes it — every editor maps to one or more RTDB nodes, and structural fields sync across all 16 locales so a reordering or a media change propagates everywhere.

Access model

  1. main.ts mounts <admin-login> when the Firebase auth session reports no user — a single Google OAuth card.
  2. Success flips to <view-cms-dashboard> — the authenticated shell with the tab strip routing between editors.
  3. Every editor writes through the Firebase SDK; parse errors and auth failures surface inline (the raw JSON editor blocks saves on malformed input so bad content can never reach the site).

Routes — the shell

FileWhat it does
main.tsCMS bundle entry — mounts login or dashboard by auth session, re-swaps on auth-changed.
routes/AdminLogin.tsx<view-admin-login> — Google OAuth gate; cancelled popups stay silent (a user action, not a failure).
routes/CmsDashboard.tsx<view-cms-dashboard> — the authenticated shell: header (brand + user + logout), tab strip between editors, toast surface.

Editors — one per content domain

Each editor follows the same facade pattern: the Cms*.tsx element owns the store and delegates to data.ts (Firebase I/O), model.ts/sections.ts (mutations), events.ts (form wiring), render.tsx (JSX), types.ts.

EditorNode(s) it edits
portfolio/CmsPortfolioList.tsxHome page's ordered project grid — item order, media dimensions, cover assignment per locale; structural fields synced across locales.
projects/CmsProjectsList.tsxFull case-study editing — project list, per-project sections (text blocks + media slots), create/delete.
about/CmsAboutEditor.tsxBio paragraphs per column, mentions list, Gravatar picture URL (with size presets).
footer/CmsFooterEditor.tsxCredit/source lines + social/other channel lists across three nodes (contact, legal-footer, related).
playground-editor/CmsPlaygroundEditor.tsxEarth-playground labels, the defaults control sub-node (initial slider/toggle values the site merges), localized route slugs.
lang/CmsLangEditor.tsxRaw JSON dictionary escape hatch — any translations node editable as formatted JSON per locale.

deploy-info/ — the quality bundle viewer

<cms-deploy-info> renders dist/deploy-info/ (written by shared/scripts/build/deploy-info.mjs at build time): Lighthouse scores per URL, Jest coverage totals, axe-core violations, Snyk/yarn-audit vulnerabilities, and the console-* governance scan — grouped into a report wall with score chips. Each report degrades independently if missing.

media-convert/ — the localhost-only media pipeline

<cms-media-converter> is a localhost-only batch converter — it exists only on the dev server (the API is a Vite plugin, never part of the built bundle). Drop a folder of images/videos in any format → files stream to a temp job dir → the tasks/* pipelines run server-side → results download as a ZIP with the site's exact CDN naming (-mozjpg*, .mp4-scaled*, MSSIM blur-up variants).

FileWhat it does
CmsMediaConverter.tsxThe drop-zone converter UI — queue, progress, ZIP download.
job.tsJob lifecycle — create → upload → convert → poll → finish.
files.tsRecursive drop/input collection (generator-based traversal) + byte formatting.
events.ts, render.tsx, consts.ts, exts.tsWiring, phase-switched templates, job phases/poll cadence, accepted extensions (shared with the node pipeline).

Required external tools (per OS)

The converter shells out to three tools; missing ones surface in the tab's tools panel (GET /api/media-convert/tools) with a copy/paste install command, and yarn setup prints the same hints before you ever open the CMS.

OSffmpeg / ffprobeImageMagickmozjpeg / cjpeg
Debian/Ubuntusudo apt-get install ffmpegsudo apt-get install imagemagicksudo apt-get install libjpeg-turbo-progs
Fedora/RHELsudo dnf install ffmpegsudo dnf install ImageMagicksudo dnf install libjpeg-turbo-utils
macOS (brew)brew install ffmpegbrew install imagemagickbrew install mozjpeg
Windows (winget)winget install -e --id Gyan.FFmpegwinget install -e --id ImageMagick.ImageMagickbundled mozjpeg via npm optional dep
Windows (choco)choco install ffmpegchoco install imagemagickchoco install mozjpeg

On Windows the converter calls magick (not convert); on macOS/Linux it calls convert. PATH must be refreshed — restart the dev server after installing.

dev/ — offline development

FileWhat it does
dev/firebase-mock.tsDev-only Firebase Auth + RTDB stub — CMS_MOCK=1 yarn dev aliases the SDK to this module. Reads the committed database.json so every editor works without credentials; writes go nowhere.

tokens/ — CMS-private vocabulary

The CMS keeps its own token tree (BEM classes, control IDs, field groups) under tokens/ — strictly isolated for the admin bundle, never imported by the public site. Grouped per feature: tokens/editors/, tokens/fields/, tokens/shell/, composed from tokens/base.ts fragments so spellings stay single-sourced.

Root files

FileWhat it does
index.tsBarrel — every editor/route element + the CMS token tree. The CMS targets ESNext only (author tool, never shipped to public visitors).
vite.config.jsLibrary build — emits cms/dist/cms.js.

Commands

yarn dev            # CMS dev server against live Firebase
CMS_MOCK=1 yarn dev # offline mode — committed database.json, no credentials needed
yarn test           # jest suite for cms
yarn build          # emits cms/dist/cms.js

Submodule of luiskr.com-V3. Install deps from the superproject (yarn install at the root), then run yarn dev / yarn test / yarn build in this folder — see package.json scripts.
